manualInputDirectoryContract.filenameDateMeaning: The date the user downloaded the CSV (not the data range).
notes: Files in this directory are placed manually by the user.
Files are never committed to the repo (manual-artifacts/ is gitignored).
Each weekly download covers the most recent ~7 trading days, but may overlap with previous weeks.
The sanitizer must handle overlap gracefully (de-duplicate by date).

expectedDownloadSource.name: NASDAQ official historical data
expectedDownloadSource.recommendedWeeklyRange: 1 month (covers last ~21 trading days; gives overlap for de-duplication)
expectedDownloadSource.recommendedInitialBackfillRange: 10 years (MAX) — one-time download to populate full history
notes: NASDAQ is the authoritative source for QQQ (Invesco ETF listed on NASDAQ).
NASDAQ download UI allows custom date range selection.
URL is recorded here for documentation only — sanitizer reads files from manualInputDirectoryContract, not from this URL.

expectedCsvFormat.headerRowLineEnding: CRLF (\r\n) per real NASDAQ CSV download

columnDescriptions.Date: US MM/DD/YYYY format (e.g. 05/11/2026). Sanitizer converts to ISO YYYY-MM-DD at import boundary.
columnDescriptions.Close/Last: Decimal price, 2 decimal places. NASDAQ column name contains a slash. Sanitizer maps this to internal name 'close'.
columnDescriptions.Volume: Non-negative integer. Not used for temperature calculation. Sanitizer may store for reference.
columnDescriptions.Open: Decimal price. May have up to 4 decimal places in real NASDAQ data (e.g. 198.0835). Not used for temperature calculation.
columnDescriptions.High: Decimal price. Not used for temperature calculation.
columnDescriptions.Low: Decimal price. Not used for temperature calculation.

expectedCsvFormat.dataRowOrder: descending (newest first) as delivered by NASDAQ
expectedCsvFormat.dataRowLineEnding: CRLF (\r\n) per real NASDAQ CSV download; sanitizer must also tolerate LF (\n) for files edited on Unix systems

dateConversionRule.interpretationLock: MUST interpret first segment as MONTH, second as DAY (US convention). Never European DD/MM/YYYY.
rejectionRules: If date does not match strict pattern ^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$, reject
If year < 2000 or > current year + 1, reject (sanity check)
dateConversionRule.rationale: M-20 design requires history to store ISO dates. The sanitizer absorbs the format difference at the import boundary.

columnMappingRule.note: Internal record uses lowercase keys with no slashes. Mapping happens during sanitization.

weeklyExtractionRule.weekDefinition: ISO 8601 week (Monday start, week 1 contains January 4)
weeklyExtractionRule.extractionMethod: For each ISO week present in the CSV, take the LAST trading day's Close (chronologically latest within that week)

outputRecordShape.date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD (the trading day used as week representative)

notes: Sanitizer outputs ASCENDING by date (oldest first) for history accumulation.
Sanitizer de-duplicates by ISO week: if multiple weekly inputs cover the same week, the most recent download wins.

plausibilityBounds.rationale: 10-year verified range: $102 - $713. Bounds set wider for future growth/decline tolerance. Out-of-range values must trigger manual review, never auto-accept.
plausibilityBounds.behaviorOnOutOfRange: Reject the row, log it for manual review, do not write to history.

rejectionScenarios.scenario: Header row does not exactly match expected
Close/Last value is empty, NaN, or non-numeric
rejectionScenarios.action: Reject the row, log it, continue with other rows
Reject the row, log it for manual review

rejectionScenarios.scenario: Date does not match MM/DD/YYYY pattern
Filename does not match yyyy-mm-dd.csv pattern
File contains rows for date > today
rejectionScenarios.action: Reject those rows (future-dated data is invalid)
